newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CREDIT SUISSE CEO DETAILS SYNERGIES.
newsitem.headline: CREDIT SUISSE CEO DETAILS SYNERGIES.

text.p: Lukas Muehlemann, chief executive officer of the Credit Suisse Group, said synergies of 300-350 million Swiss francs ($200-230 million) from merging with Winterthur Group was based on a "rather conservative estimate" of collaboration so far between the two.

In a speech released ahead of a joint news conference, Muehlemann provided following details of the synergies: -- In Switzerland earnings can be increased by at least 70 to 90 million francs, in particular through full access to each other's sales channels. -- On the cost side in Switzerland, synergies amount to at least 130-150 million francs, primarily from better use of office premises, reduced information technology and telecommunications costs and the integration of CS Life into Winterthur Life. -- Outside Switzerland, earnings should rise at least 25 to 30 million francs, primarily through joint development of the personal financial services and employee benefit business in growth markets such as southern Europe and Asia. -- In business with major international corporate clients, there is considerable potential in the area of structured transactions and in employee benefit business. Additional income of at least 10-20 million francs is estimated. -- On the asset management side, synergies of 30-35 million francs are estimated by leveraging the best skills in the Group and preferred provider synergies are estimated at 15-20 million. -- There is a potential of more than 20 million francs from optimisation of capital management.
